title: Aldehyde or Ketone? The Distinguishing Tests
subject: Chemistry
objective: Two colourless compounds, both with C=O. How Tollens', Fehling's and the iodoform test tell an aldehyde from a ketone, and why they work.

fill.q: In an aldehyde the carbonyl carbon carries a ____ atom.
Tollens' test gives a silver ____ with aldehydes.
In Fehling's test aliphatic aldehydes give a brick-red precipitate of ____.
The yellow precipitate in the iodoform test is ____.
The iodoform test detects the ____ group.

tf.q: Ketones are easily oxidised by Tollens' reagent.
Benzaldehyde gives Tollens' test but generally not Fehling's test.
tf.explain: Aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's solution.

tf.q: In Tollens' test the aldehyde is reduced.
tf.explain: The aldehyde is oxidised; Ag⁺ is reduced.

ar.r: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylate ions.

ar.explain: A is true; propanone is a ketone.

short.q: Suggest tests to distinguish propanal from propanone.
short.solution: Tollens': propanal gives a silver mirror, propanone does not (also Fehling's: propanal brick red; iodoform: propanone yellow CHI₃).

match.explain: Each test matches its positive sign.
